title: Chat event sink shims and ergonomic recipe library for Python SDK streaming
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: teams building streaming chat UIs repeatedly implement similar plumbing: incremental partial-event assembly, merging role/content deltas, safe shutdown checkpoints, and different consumer ergonomics for sync vs async code paths. This ticket creates a small, batteries-included recipe library in the Python SDK that surface-level simplifies those patterns via 'sink shims' -- tiny adapters that accept raw stream events and emit well-formed messages, flush signals, and developer-friendly backpressure hooks.
background: We've seen multiple internal and customer bugs where partial 'delta' events lead to duplicate UI flashes, or app-level retries accidentally replay the same partial response causing incoherent output. Current example apps in repo/ are ad hoc and often confuse teams integrating streaming. A compact SDK-level set of patterns (shims + examples) will reduce duplicated code and make best-practices discoverable.
proposal: Deliver a Python-only library (module: redwood.sdk.streaming.recipes) that includes: 1) EventSinkShim: synchronous adapter for callback-based consumers that reconstructs messages from deltas and emits completion events; 2) AsyncStreamSink: asyncio-friendly async iterator wrapper that exposes an iteration of completed chunks and exposes 'drain_to_checkpoint()' for graceful shutdown; 3) IdempotentSink: optional layer that deduplicates idempotent chunks using message ids and watermarking; 4) RetrySurface: configurable retry hooks for transient network/error spikes that preserve partial reassembly state. Provide three canonical examples: console-progress demo, Flask SSE server, and an asyncio websocket relay. Keep API intentionally small and documented with migration guide from existing ad-hoc patterns.
api_examples:
# sync consumer shim example:
from redwood.sdk.streaming.recipes import EventSinkShim

sink = EventSinkShim(on_message=lambda msg: print(msg['content']), on_done=lambda: print('done'))

# underlying stream calls sink.accept(event) for each event chunk
# sink coalesces deltas and calls on_message only for completed deltas or meaningful interim updates

# async iterator example:
import asyncio
from redwood.sdk.streaming.recipes import AsyncStreamSink

async def consume(stream):
    async for chunk in AsyncStreamSink.from_stream(stream, progressive_updates=True):
        # chunk is a dict { 'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'partial or full', 'is_final': bool }
        await process_chunk(chunk)

# graceful shutdown: await sink.drain_to_checkpoint() to persist partial state before closing

# idempotent sink / retry example:
sink = IdempotentSink(inner=EventSinkShim(...), watermark_policy='last-commit')
# when the SDK performs an automated retry, IdempotentSink prevents re-emitting already-acknowledged chunks
acceptance_criteria: Publish redwood.sdk.streaming.recipes module with documented EventSinkShim, AsyncStreamSink, and IdempotentSink APIs
Include three runnable examples (console, Flask SSE, asyncio websocket) in examples/ with README and small test harnesses
Add unit tests covering delta reassembly, out-of-order partials, and idempotent deduplication with >90% branch coverage for new code
Add one integration test that exercises backpressure by simulating slow consumer and verifies drain_to_checkpoint flush behavior
Doc PR reviewed and signed off by SDK lead and PM

notes: Design trade-offs: keeping API small vs supporting all edge-cases. We favor small, composable adapters that can be extended rather than a monolithic stream manager.
Performance: keep shim overhead minimal (<0.2ms per event on p3-like instance) by avoiding deep copies; add microbenchmarks in tests/benchmarks
Migration: provide wrapper helpers so teams can swap their existing on_delta handlers with EventSinkShim without changing business logic
Follow-ups: consider a TypeScript parity project to match the same recipes for the JS SDK
